instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: No Tie Stands
cards.instruction: Turn every even outcome into a formal rematch with a new rule and a consequence for losing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put zeros beside our cakes, like you. A tie. Rematch without icing; loser washes the tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those zeros mean I haven't entered the judge's scores yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, provisional results. We'll settle it on one bite each.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The judge gave us nine each. She said the icing was what she liked best.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then an official nine-all. Icing only for the decider, and the loser washes every spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ten pounds each. I've put my bank card face down like yours. Rematch: loser pays the tip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's face down so nobody reads the number. We're paying for dinner, not playing cards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, private entries. Turn them over; higher last digit wins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not showing you my card. I'll toss a coin for the tip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Best of three. Call before each toss, and the loser pays the whole tip. No splitting it again.

cards.title: Every Loss Builds the Comeback
cards.instruction: Treat each setback as proof that the eventual victory will be more impressive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three penalties will make our trophy photo better. I blew my whistle whenever the referee did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You aren't a referee. They penalized us because you kept stopping play.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, making a comeback worth watching. Wait till I lead us out of last place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The team has asked me to captain. They still want you cheering from the sideline.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A comeback without even being captain. Save me a place beside you in that trophy photo; people will want the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stood when you stood, ready for our encore. They'll remember this audition when I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stood because the piano pedal snapped. We haven't even finished your song.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a dramatic pause. The recovery will be the part the judges remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll have to finish without piano. I can give you the starting note.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give it to me. When I win with no accompaniment, make sure they know I started with a broken piano.

cards.title: Congratulate Through Your Teeth
cards.instruction: Perform warm praise while allowing competitive resentment to intensify beneath every compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I clapped when the chair did. Congratulations. Lovely to see you getting your turn at last.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She was clapping to quiet the room. You were the only one applauding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Getting in early. You deserve a moment without all that competition around you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you stand beside me for the winner's photograph? I want you in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. How generous to fit someone without a prize into your winner's photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've boxed my desk things like you. Congratulations on the promotion. You make moving up look wonderfully simple.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm packing because I get the corner office. You still work here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, making room for you. How lovely to get a door between yourself and the rest of us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Leave your things out. I'll ask them to give you my bigger desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How kind. More room for my next unsuccessful application.

cards.title: Nothing Without Stakes
cards.instruction: Price every request and decision with a reward, penalty, bargain, or trade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hands up, like you. I'll say sorry for losing your keys if you stop calling me careless.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I put my hands up because you threw my coat at me. I wasn't surrendering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, returning property. I'll pick it up if you take back careless.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pick it up and apologize. Then I'll admit I shouldn't have shouted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your admission with the apology, not after. I'll give you the coat as we say them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I folded the ladder the way you did. First sausage for me, and I'll bring it over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine folds when I pull the pin. You've bent the brace on yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right, a firmer fold. Help me straighten it and you can have it for two sausages.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't climb that. Help me carry mine instead and I'll give you first choice off the grill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First choice twice. Once for carrying, once for leaving you my ladder's space in the shed.

cards.title: Fair Means I Can Win
cards.instruction: Agree to any rule or bargain only after interpreting fairness in a way that preserves your advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've joined you up here. A fair starting position for the race.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the starter. I stand ahead so the runners can see my flag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely. I should see it just as clearly as everyone else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stand anywhere on that line. You're all racing to the oak tree over on the left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the left end is mine. Same line for everyone; no need to equalize the distance as well.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took a rose off the cake when you took one. Now cut us equal slices.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was plastic. I was removing the decorations. You ate an icing rose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the top. Equal slices after preparation is only fair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then your slice comes from the bare patch. Mine can have the remaining icing rose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal means matching decoration. Cut the last rose in half before I agree to the slices.
